name: Mary Slessor
title: Mary Slessor: learning to care far from home
description: From the mills of Dundee to Calabar: a look at Mary Slessor, her service, and the limits of the missionary biographies of her time.

sections.heading: From Dundee to Calabar
paragraphs: Mary Slessor was born in Scotland in 1848 and worked from a young age in the mills of Dundee. Her church life nurtured her interest in mission. In 1876 she traveled to Calabar, in the territory that is now part of Nigeria, sent by the Scottish Presbyterian mission.

The biography by W. P. Livingstone describes how she learned the language, her health problems, and her adjustment to local life. It is a work close to her own time and written with admiration. It helps us follow her path, although its language and cultural judgments call for careful reading.

sections.heading: Real people behind the story
paragraphs: Slessor is remembered for taking in children whose lives were threatened, among them twins, and for her part in resolving conflicts. The account includes Ma Eme and other people from the communities where she lived. Her local relationships were an essential part of what made her caregiving and her daily work possible.

Reading this story requires us to distinguish between protecting particular lives and making generalizations about entire peoples. The mission took place in a context of British colonial expansion. The biographer’s categories should not automatically become our description of African communities, nor should they erase those communities’ own initiative.

reflection: In James 2:15–17, faith shows itself in meeting real needs. The question for a Christian community can be very concrete: what happens after we tell someone that God loves them? A child needs protection, a family needs support, and a sick person needs care they are able to receive.

A willingness to serve must go hand in hand with listening and learning. Loving our neighbor includes recognizing their voice, their story, and their abilities. The memory of Slessor can encourage us to care with perseverance and to examine the attitudes of superiority that are sometimes mixed in with good intentions.
review_note: The biography is read as a testimony of its time, without adopting its colonial vocabulary or presenting Slessor as the only agent of change. No figures for rescues are included.
source_labels: W. P. Livingstone. Mary Slessor of Calabar: Pioneer Missionary (1915), Project Gutenberg digital edition.
source_kinds: Historical biography from a missionary perspective
